scenarios.title: The First Big Purchase
scenarios.text: You can finally afford the car you've wanted since high school.

choices.label: Buy it and show {parent}
choices.result: You buy it and drive it home first. {parent} won't stop smiling.

choices.label: Buy something sensible
choices.result: You buy something sensible and put the rest away. It's a good car. It isn't the car.

choices.label: Wait a year
choices.result: You wait a year. The want fades a little, and so does the fun.

scenarios.title: The Regional Endorsement
scenarios.text: A regional company offers you a sponsorship worth more than your rookie salary.

choices.label: Sign it
choices.result: You sign it. The shoots take some weekends, and the money is real.

choices.label: Read the fine print
choices.result: You read the fine print and strike two clauses. They agree.

choices.label: Pass on it
choices.result: You pass. Your weekends stay yours.

scenarios.title: The Investment Pitch
scenarios.text: A man at a charity dinner pitches you an investment: guaranteed returns, a famous partner, no risk. He's done this before, and he knows you can tell.

choices.label: Walk away
choices.result: You thank him and walk away. Six months later you read his name in the paper, and you pass the article to your teammates.

choices.label: Ask someone you trust
choices.result: You show it to someone you trust. They laugh, then explain exactly how it works. You learn more in an hour than in a year of statements.

choices.label: Put money in
choices.result: You put money in. The statements look great for a while, then they stop coming, and so does he. The shame lasts longer than the loss.

scenarios.title: The Rookie Mentor
scenarios.text: The club asks you to help a younger player adjust, the way someone helped you.

choices.label: Take it on
choices.result: You agree to it: meals, film, the long drives. He's steadier by midseason.

choices.label: Be a friend
choices.result: You keep it friendly instead of formal. He calls you when it matters.

choices.label: Point him elsewhere
choices.result: You point him to a veteran with more time.

scenarios.title: The Locker Room Reputation
scenarios.text: Younger teammates have started looking at you when something goes wrong.

choices.label: Step into it
choices.result: You step into it. When the room gets loud, you're the calm voice.

choices.label: Pick your moments
choices.result: You speak rarely and choose the moments. They listen more for it.

choices.label: Stay a kicker
choices.result: You stay a kicker. There are captains for that.

scenarios.title: The Coaching Change
scenarios.text: A new special teams coach arrives with a new way of doing everything.

choices.label: Try it all
choices.result: You try every new drill without complaint. Some of it helps.

choices.label: Pick what works
choices.result: You keep what works and explain why the rest doesn't. He respects the reasoning.

choices.label: Get to know him
choices.result: You get to know him before you judge the drills.

scenarios.title: The Public Relationship
scenarios.text: Your relationship becomes a topic of public interest, and {love_interest} didn't sign up for that.

choices.label: Protect {love_interest}
choices.result: You stop posting about home entirely. {love_interest} notices and is grateful.

choices.label: Set boundaries together
choices.result: You agree together on what stays private and what doesn't.

choices.label: Let it blow over
choices.result: You let it blow over. It takes longer than you thought.

scenarios.title: The First Home Repair
scenarios.text: The roof leaks the week of a road trip, and the bill is enormous.

choices.label: Handle it by phone
choices.result: You handle it by phone from the hotel. It gets done, expensively.

choices.label: Ask {parent} to oversee it
choices.result: You ask {parent} to oversee the repair. They love being useful.

choices.label: Patch it for now
choices.result: You patch it for now and deal with it in the offseason.

scenarios.title: The Charity Commitment
scenarios.text: A nonprofit asks you to become a regular supporter, not just a photo.

choices.label: Commit for real
choices.result: You commit to monthly visits. The kids know your name by spring.

choices.label: Bring teammates
choices.result: You bring teammates along. It becomes a team tradition.

choices.label: Stay a donor
choices.result: You write a check and stay a donor.

scenarios.title: The Radio Segment
scenarios.text: You're offered a recurring weekly segment on sports radio.

choices.label: Take it
choices.result: You say yes. You're good at it, and your Tuesdays disappear.

choices.label: Try it for a month
choices.result: You sign up for a month and then decide. You keep it, shorter.

choices.label: Decline
choices.result: You decline. You'd rather talk about kicking with kickers.

scenarios.title: The Offseason Vacation
scenarios.text: {love_interest} wants a real vacation; you want to train.

choices.label: Go on the vacation
choices.result: You go, and you don't bring a ball. It's the best week of the year.

choices.label: Train instead
choices.result: You train. {love_interest} goes with friends and sends pictures.

choices.label: Find a place with a field
choices.result: You find a beach town with a high school field. Everyone wins, sort of.

scenarios.title: The Former Teammate
scenarios.text: A former teammate can't find another job in the league and keeps calling.

choices.label: Keep picking up
choices.result: You keep picking up. Mostly he needs someone to listen.

choices.label: Help him find work
choices.result: You call people you know about jobs outside football. One works out.

choices.label: Let it go to voicemail
choices.result: You let it go to voicemail sometimes. You feel bad about it.

scenarios.title: The New Neighborhood
scenarios.text: You can get involved in your neighborhood or stay a stranger on your own street.

choices.label: Knock on doors
choices.result: You introduce yourself up and down the street. The neighbors bring food after a loss.

choices.label: Help with the youth league
choices.result: You help coach the neighborhood youth league once a week.

choices.label: Keep to yourself
choices.result: You keep to yourself. It's quiet, and a little lonely.
